flawed_step: Line 0012 assumes that relaxing (v,u) during iteration k+1 uses a dist[v] representing a path with at most k edges. With in-place relaxations, dist[v] may already have been improved earlier in the same iteration, so longer paths can propagate.
counterexample: Let the directed edges, relaxed in this order, be s->a of weight 1, a->w of weight 1, and s->w of weight 10. Initially dist[s]=0 and the others are infinity. During the first iteration, relaxing s->a gives dist[a]=1; relaxing a->w then gives dist[w]=2; relaxing s->w leaves dist[w]=2. Yet the smallest length of an s-to-w path having at most one edge is 10. Thus after k=1 iteration, dist[w]=2 rather than the claimed value 10.
assessment_summary: The exact at-most-k-edges claim is false for ordinary in-place Bellman–Ford passes because multiple improvements can cascade within one pass. It would hold for synchronous iterations that read exclusively from the previous iteration’s distance array.
